captions: English burned into the video; companion SRT
scope: Original schematic animation, not a recording or a cycle-accurate simulation.

chapters.title: Three places to follow
chapters.caption: HBM holds the data. L2 holds temporary cached copies. SMs run the GPU kernels.

chapters.title: A previous GEMM leaves cached copies
chapters.caption: A and B are still in HBM. Some copies of their data also remain in L2.

chapters.title: Prepare a cold-input benchmark
chapters.caption: We want to displace those cached copies before timing the next GEMM. We do not delete A or B.

chapters.title: Read-only eviction: stream unrelated data
chapters.caption: A GPU kernel reads a separate 512 MiB buffer. These reads replace earlier A/B copies in the 60 MiB L2.

chapters.title: The read kernel finishes
chapters.caption: The large buffer is unchanged. Its cached copies are clean. Only 4 KiB of checksum results are written.

chapters.title: Now start timing the GEMM
chapters.caption: The GEMM brings A/B back from HBM. Unrelated clean cache lines can be discarded without writeback.

chapters.title: Same starting point; change the preparation
chapters.caption: Rewind to the same A/B data. This time, the preparation reads AND modifies the unrelated buffer.

chapters.title: Write-based eviction leaves some dirty lines
chapters.caption: Modified copies are newer than their HBM backing data. Some remain in L2 after preparation ends.

chapters.title: The next GEMM causes extra writeback
chapters.caption: Replacing those dirty lines generates writes to HBM alongside the GEMM reads. The GEMM does the same math.

chapters.title: Hardware counters show the extra traffic
chapters.caption: HBM reads and GEMM instruction counts match. Write-based preparation produces many more HBM writes.

chapters.title: Eviction changes the cache state
chapters.caption: Eviction removes cached copies, not the original data. Clean copies can be dropped; dirty copies need writeback.
